anchors.paper_title: MNE-BIDS: Organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format and facilitating their analysis
anchors.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
anchors.reason: MNE-BIDS is a software tool for organizing electrophysiology data into BIDS, used to format the dataset, not a paper describing the MET music-induced EEG data.

anchors.paper_title: EEG-BIDS, an extension to the brain imaging data structure for electroencephalography
anchors.reason: The paper specifies the EEG-BIDS standard that the dataset follows for organization. It does not describe the MET music-induced EEG dataset.

metadata.methods_description: EEG was recorded with a 128-channel system at 1000 Hz. After preprocessing and channel selection, 66 channels were retained. Each participant completed one resting-state session and twenty music-listening sessions of 130 s each (5 s pre-onset, 120 s music, 5 s post-offset). Data are stored in BrainVision format.
